ops.title: Controller-open desired-set recovery replays stale agents destructively and fatally — fixed releases cannot supersede their own failed-era state
ops.description:
Field evidence (yasyf-home, 2026-07-26, synckit 0.36.3 on daemonkit v0.20.8; fleet task fc39f885, investigation 8841b9c0): `synckitd install` failed at `service: recover desired set: service: install agent "com.github.yasyf.synckit.helper.reposync": launchctl bootstrap ... EIO`. The controller's open-path recovery replayed the persisted services.db Desired entry — the OLD Background-keyed, Caskroom-path agent recorded by the original failed install — before install()'s body could compute fresh agents from current manifests. The replay REWROTE the on-disk plist back to the keyed version (destroying a working manually-bootstrapped interim fix), booted out the running helper, failed the same EIO, and aborted the open — so the fixed release's emission was never even exercised.

Two defects compound: (1) FATALITY — recovery failure aborts the open, so install can never reach the code that would supersede the stale entry with a fresh, fixed computation; the machine is wedged until the stale entry is removed by hand. (2) DESTRUCTIVENESS — the replay's bootout-before-bootstrap tears down whatever was running; a failed recovery leaves the service DOWN, strictly worse than before the attempt, on every controller open.

Sibling of the applyRolledBack reconciliation gap (fixed in v0.20.8, deployment/apply.go): both are self-delivery wedges where persisted state from the failed era blocks the fix that would clear it. A common shape may cover both: treat a failed replay of a stale entry as reportable drift rather than fatal, let the incoming operation's fresh computation supersede, and never bootout a running agent until its replacement has proven viable.

ops.text: A stale persisted Desired entry whose replay fails does not prevent install() from computing and converging fresh agents from current inputs
Recovery never tears down a running agent it cannot replace (bootout only after the replacement bootstrap is proven viable, or failure leaves the prior running)
A machine wedged with a failed-era Desired entry converges on upgrade without manual state surgery
